title: OpenAPI 3.1 generated from source and served alongside interactive documentation
asA: API consumer evaluating and integrating the service
iWant: a machine-readable spec and browsable documentation generated from the code that is actually running
soThat: what I read is what the service does, with no hand-maintained copy to drift

acceptanceCriteria.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document is produced from implementation source at build time; the repository contains no hand-written parallel spec that requires separate editing.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the OpenAPI document is emitted as a build artefact derived from source annotations or route definitions, and no hand-maintained duplicate exists

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /openapi.json returns the generated spec as application/json and GET /openapi.yaml returns the same spec as YAML; the two are semantically identical.
acceptanceCriteria.then: both return 200 with correct content types and parse to the same specification

acceptanceCriteria.description: GET /docs serves interactive documentation rendered from the same generated spec, listing every endpoint with its schemas and auth class.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documentation UI renders from the served spec and every endpoint in the spec is browsable

acceptanceCriteria.description: The generated document validates as OpenAPI 3.1: an off-the-shelf validator accepts it with zero errors.
acceptanceCriteria.when: an OpenAPI 3.1 validator runs against it

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every operation in the generated spec carries an operationId, a summary, request and response schemas, and the x-auth-class extension; no operation ships undocumented.
acceptanceCriteria.then: operationId, summary, schemas, and x-auth-class are present on every operation

acceptanceCriteria.description: The documentation endpoints (/openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /docs) respond according to the project's declared exposure policy, and in non-production environments they are always available.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the declared exposure policy and a non-production deployment
acceptanceCriteria.then: responses match the declared policy, and the non-production deployment serves all three
